claim_verdicts.claim: E34's order-24 'step shortfall' was sampling noise
claim_verdicts.evidence: The walk is E34's: with the fix off the E41 code reproduces all 1,280 E34 Stage R records byte for byte (replayed twice here: all 1,280 walks through the validator driver against the E34 files with the validator comparator, 1,280 / 1,280 byte-identical, and the rebuilt e41_run identity stage, whose identity.json and identity.log equal the committed ones byte for byte). E34's 16-seed records give steps ratio 1.7009 (order 6 0.9239 ± 0.0457, order 24 1.0864 ± 0.0451 of the ideal; z = 2.70 below 2). On fresh seeds it is 1.9270 ± 0.0439 (main stream, z = 1.66) and 1.9647 ± 0.0451 (against the A/A stream, z = 0.78); E41's 95 % interval [1.841, 2.013] excludes 1.701. The deviation from 2 falls from 0.299 to 0.073 and 0.035 as walks per curve and order go from 16 to 128, as noise must; ratio-of-sums weighting gives the same picture (1.766 -> 1.981, 1.970). Pooling every walk of each order: 1.950 ± 0.031. Stage 0 finds no order-24-specific cause (fruitless revisits 0.84·10⁻⁴ a step for order 24 against 3.57·10⁻⁴ for order 6, redirects 1/32 in both, no distinguished-point losses). Caveat: E34's draw was an unlucky one (2.7 SE from the ideal, 1.9 SE from E41's estimate), and E41's own main-stream ratio still sits 1.7 SE below 2 because its order-6 arm ran short (0.969; G2.219 falsified, as reported); 'noise' here means 'not reproduced by eight times the walks on two fresh streams'.

heuristic_validation_checks.result: The ideal sqrt(pi (n - 1)/(2m)) (expected steps to the first repeat of a random mapping on (n - 1)/m classes) and G2.216-G2.229 with numeric bounds were committed in f99a56359e (2026-11-02T18:15:10Z), before the fix code (b0e307d9b8, 18:17:54Z) and every registered record (files written 19:01-19:25Z, committed b70f356827 19:36:14Z). §9.52 at HEAD is byte-identical to its registered text (only a trailing newline before §9.53 was added). Stage 0 (seeds 41000+k, instrument 089f7f7823/6115e0ea0a) was run before the registration and openly shaped it; the registered streams (48000+k, 49000+k) are disjoint from it.

Seeds, curve, arm, arithmetic and jump table are in every record; layout checked (8 curves in E18's order, seeds 48000-48127 / 49000-49127 / 48000-48031, five arms seed-major). The empirical steps/ideal and every band ratio are recomputed from the 7,424 per-walk records, not copied: O6B 0.9694 ± 0.0159, O24 1.0061 ± 0.0159, O24F 0.9986 ± 0.0163, O24' 0.9868 ± 0.0158 (1,024 walks each); E34's records 0.9239 ± 0.0457 and 1.0864 ± 0.0451 (128 each); Stage 0 1.0265 ± 0.0226 and 1.0382 ± 0.0228 (512 each).

The A/A arm O24' (the same walk on a disjoint seed stream) is the null object for any between-arm difference: O24/O24' = 1.0185 / 1.0192 / 1.0195 with 95 % intervals [0.976, 1.061], [0.975, 1.063], [0.975, 1.064], not resolved, and it sets the registered floor. For the shortfall itself the parameter that should destroy a noise artifact is the number of walks: 2 - (steps ratio) falls from 0.299 (16 walks per curve and order, z = 2.70 from 2) to 0.073 (128, main stream, z = 1.66) and 0.035 (128, A/A stream, z = 0.78); a real 15 % order-24 shortfall would not shrink (E41's interval [1.841, 2.013] excludes E34's 1.701). It decays as a noise artifact should.

No substitute sampler: the walks themselves are measured. The class sizes m = 6 and 24 rest on E29's kill test (order-24 group <lambda_p, lambda_omega, -1>) and its validation; this validator checked independently that every n is prime and n = 1 mod 24 (own Miller-Rabin), and that the recorded ideal equals sqrt(pi floor((n - 1)/m)/2) on every walk (max relative difference 0).

p = 241-1069 (n = 2^31.65 to 2^40.25), 128 walks per curve and arm schoolbook, 32 Karatsuba, one stream each plus the A/A stream. The steps ideal is asymptotic in n; the per-step cost ratios (representative cost against walk cost) are counts that do not depend on n, but nothing here measures n beyond 2^40.3. The E18 handover shift (bits) is a model consequence (4 log2 of the factor applied to a modelled handover), not a measurement.

cost_model_checks.result: F_p multiplications (jump table, start point, the cheap arms' tables and F's added additions included; the [d]G = Q check excluded, verify_fp_muls subtracted on every arm) plus w · 97 · (cmp + neg + modn + hash + table), w = 0, 0.1, 1; the same unit as E34 (§9.38).

F adds, per walk, exactly 32 group additions whose F_p multiplications are counted in fp_muls (3,104 = 32 × 97 schoolbook on all 1,024 + 32 control walks, 2,528 = 32 × 79 Karatsuba on all 256) and 64 mod-n additions counted in walk.ops.modn (native, priced at w · 97); nothing per step: the partition is still one hash per evaluation (mod 64 instead of mod 32), the look-ahead one table read. Every E34-jump walk adds 0. The 32 extra jump points' memory is not priced (32 F_p4 points per walk).

The band prices native work at 97 F_p multiplications in both arithmetics, as registered; Karatsuba's own addition costs 79. At 79: O6B/O24 1.711 / 1.391 / 1.253, O6C/O24 1.635 / 1.290 / 1.141, O24/O24F 0.984 / 0.981 / 0.980: the same orders.

Not priced. Every arm stores every visited class (exhaustive storage, no distinguished points; stored + fruitless + 1 = steps on every correct walk), so memory is proportional to steps and the order-24 walk stores about 1.93× fewer classes than the order-6 walk; no time-memory trade-off is claimed.
Every walk succeeds (7,424 / 7,424 correct), so the expected cost is the mean per-walk cost; no success-probability factor is involved.

A reference correction and a re-measurement (G2.229): rho walks only. No E41 commit touches docs/ic/, docs/ic-leaderboard.html or benchmarks/; §9.52, §9.53 and REPORT.typ state the class; the GLS IC rows keep factor 1; no index-calculus cost or improvement is claimed.

inventor_protocol_ladder: Not a speedup claim for an index-calculus method: the measured quantity (order-24 walk against order-6 walks) is a ratio measured directly at the tested scale, with an A/A null arm and a broken-fix positive control. The only extrapolations are labelled as derived: the E18 handover shift in bits and the distance factor applied to E18's modelled psi rows.
observations: The planted logarithm is 271 on all eight curves (E29's instances); every one of the 7,424 walks recovers it and ran the [d]G = Q check (verify counters > 0), and the replayed walks reproduce those fields byte for byte.

Same walk on the paired arms: O6C equals O6B, and O24L equals O24, seed by seed (steps, escapes, visit digest, logarithm); only the representative's counted work differs. Karatsuba walks equal the schoolbook walks of the same seed in every counter except F_p multiplications.

Pooling every walk of each order (E34's records, Stage 0, the main stream and, for order 24, the A/A stream): order 6 at 0.9835 ± 0.0125 of its ideal (1,664 walks), order 24 at 1.0087 ± 0.0098 (2,688 walks), steps ratio 1.950 ± 0.031 (1.6 SE below 2). E41's residual ratio deficit comes from the order-6 arm running short on the main stream (0.969), not from an order-24 excess; per-curve heterogeneity is within noise (sum of squared per-curve z: O6B 12.6, O24 11.0, O24' 3.6, O24F 6.6 on 8 degrees of freedom; 95 % point 15.5).

Per curve the order-6/order-24 ranking uses the registered point-estimate rule; with each curve's own 95 % interval required at every weight, O6B/O24 is resolved on 6 of 8 curves (not p = 241, 337) and O6C/O24 on 5 of 8 (not p = 241, 337, 1069); p = 241 changes order on O6C/O24 at 1 GAE (1.413 / 1.128 / 0.995).

The seed-paired delta method (the arms share seeds on the main stream) gives 95 % intervals within 0.001 of the independent ones on the schoolbook headline pairs (within 0.008 in Karatsuba, 32 walks) and changes no rank across the band. Only O24L / O24, which is one walk under two representatives, moves: its paired SE is near 0, so its registered-rule flag turns true in Karatsuba too, while the order still changes inside the band (not ranked).
F's step saving is estimator-dependent in sign (mean over walks -0.75 %, ratio of sums +2.8 %, per curve 4 / 4): nothing distinguishes F from no change, as registered (G2.222).
E41's three local-only records match their committed .sha256 files, and stage0_run.json also equals its blob at f99a56359e (it was committed there and untracked in f0eb95af97).

The report's figures script (figures/plot.py) lays out values from summary.json, stage0_records.json and stage0_run.json; its only arithmetic is error-bar extents and offsets for plotting. The leaderboard, benchmarks/ and the gate were not touched by any E41 commit.
limitations: Local container (4 vCPU, shared with E39 and E40), not isolab-eks (no aws CLI or kubectl here); operation counts only, no wall time compared.

The in-crate unit tests (twist24_shortfall::tests, E34's twist24_rep test) were not run: release unit-test builds are excluded on this host (memory). The replayed identity (1,280 / 1,280 E34 records, both through the rebuilt binary and through the validator's own comparator) covers what e41_instrument_is_e34s_walk asserts; the pair-sum test's assertions (32 added additions, 64 mod-n, correct log, the broken control wrong) are covered by the records and the replayed control.

e41_stage0 (6115e0ea0a) was not rebuilt (a second full crypto_lib build on a shared host); its records' content was replayed for 32 nonce-drawn walks through the b0e307d9b8 library, whose fix-off path is the same walk.

main_school.json, main_karatsuba.json and stage0_run.json are not in Git (no aws CLI for the artifact store); they are pinned by committed .sha256 files, which the local copies match, and this replay regenerated them from committed code (see the certificate's whole-file runs). The validator's own replay outputs over 64 KiB are likewise kept local and pinned by SHA-256 in the certificate.
The E18 psi-row factor applies to modelled distances (E18's psi arm is linear algebra with a modelled handover, §9.3); the handover shift in bits is a model consequence, not a measurement.

The order-24 group itself is not recomputed from curve coefficients (they are not in E41's records); it rests on E29's kill test and its validation, as for E34. n prime and n = 1 mod 24 were checked here.
Scale: n from 2^31.65 to 2^40.25 only; nothing here measures larger n.
